story.title: The Knocking Inside the Walls at 2:48

narrator.persona: a night-shift locksmith telling it a year later

sentences.text: In our town, the old people say three knocks at midnight mean the dead are testing the latch.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: Every single night at exactly two forty-eight, heavy fist blows echo from my front door.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: I checked the peephole last week, and the porch light showed only an empty mat.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: Tonight the wet thuds came from inside the living room wallpaper.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: My terrified brother whispered from the dark hallway, Open it.
sentences.speaker: person

sentences.text: When I looked in the hall mirror, I saw it tumbling sideways across the floorboards like a boneless wolf with violet eyes.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: Would you have stayed in that room?
sentences.speaker: narrator
